metaDesc: How to day-trip from Bangkok to Lopburi's old town by train with no overnight stay. Train times, ticket prices, a walking route through Phra Prang Sam Yot, King Narai's Palace and Vichayen House, plus where to eat and how to dodge the monkeys.

h1:
Bangkok to Lopburi
by Train: Old Town in a Day
intro: Lopburi is one of the few places you can reach by train from Bangkok, see in a morning, and be back the same evening with no overnight stay. The station sits right in the middle of the old town, so the moment you step off the platform you're staring at Phra Prang Sam Yot and a troop of monkeys. King Narai's Palace, Vichayen House and the old-school restaurants are all within walking distance. This is a day-trip plan I've actually walked, and it doesn't wear you out.
chips: 🚂 There and back in a day
🚶 Walk it all from the station

blocks.html: What makes Lopburi work for Bangkok folks is that it's close and easy. It's around 150 km from Bangkok, roughly 2.5 to 3 hours by train, and Lopburi station happens to sit in the heart of the old town. Unlike a lot of cities where the station is way out from the centre, here you step off and start sightseeing on foot with no transfers. It's perfect if you want to escape the city for a dose of history without doing a lot of planning.

blocks.text: How to take the train to Lopburi — times and prices

blocks.html: Northern long-distance trains now mostly leave from Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal (Bang Sue). Lopburi sits on the northern line, so every train passes through it — morning, midday and evening, with plenty of departures to choose from. Third-class tickets are dirt cheap, starting at just a few tens of baht, while rapid and express trains with comfier seats cost a bit more but are still around the low hundreds. The key thing for a day trip is to pick a morning train that reaches Lopburi before noon, and book your evening return in advance.

items: Recommended outbound train — pick one leaving Bangkok in the morning (around 6–8 am) so you reach Lopburi before noon and have a full day to walk around.
Journey time — about 2.5 to 3 hours depending on the train type. Express trains are a little quicker than ordinary ones.
Ticket prices — third class starts in the tens of baht, while rapid and special express trains with better seats run around the low hundreds.
Book ahead — check times and book on the State Railway's d-ticket site (dticket.railway.co.th), especially the busy evening return trains.

blocks.title: Always check the timetable first
blocks.html: Train schedules change from time to time and some departures get retimed. Before you go, check the State Railway site (railway.co.th) for the latest times on your travel date, and build in a little buffer for delays. Don't book your return train too tight.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Lopburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Lopburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: A one-day plan walking the old town around the station

blocks.html: Lopburi's best feature is that all the main sights sit inside an old-town zone you can walk in under 2 km. Step out of the station, turn a corner, and there's Phra Prang Sam Yot. Walk a little further and you reach King Narai's Palace, Vichayen House and Phra Kan Shrine. The whole thing loops back to the station perfectly. This is the order that keeps you from backtracking.

blocks.label: Done in a day
blocks.title: Off the train, walk the old town, back on the train

items.activity: Arrive at Lopburi station, drop your bag at left luggage, and start walking
items.note: The station has a luggage drop, though if you've only got a small bag you can just carry it. Step out the front of the station and you'll see the prang almost directly across the road.

items.activity: Grab lunch at an old-town spot and fuel up before you set off
items.note: Along Narai Maharat Road and around the station there are several long-running noodle and rice shops. Eating before you walk out into the sun makes the day a lot more comfortable.

items.activity: Phra Prang Sam Yot — the landmark right across from the station
items.note: Entry is 10 THB for Thais. It's the three-towered Khmer temple that's become Lopburi's signature image. Lots of monkeys hang around here, so keep an eye on your valuables.

items.activity: Phra Kan Shrine — an old shrine right next door
items.note: Just a short walk from the prang, it's another monkey hotspot. You can take photos, but don't carry plastic bags or hold food out in the open.

items.activity: King Narai's Palace (Phra Narai Ratchaniwet) — wander a palace from King Narai's reign
items.note: Entry is 30 THB for Thais, open 9:00–16:30. The Somdet Phra Narai Museum is inside the palace grounds. The site is wide and shady, and you'll want about an hour to walk it.

items.activity: Vichayen House (the ambassadors' residence) — ruins blending Western and Thai styles
items.note: Open Wednesday–Sunday, so it's shut on Monday and Tuesday — check the day before you go. The old brick ruins make for some nice atmospheric photos.

items.activity: Find dinner or a cafe near the station, then catch the train back
items.note: Loop back toward the station, stop at a cafe or grab something to eat before your evening train, and aim to reach the station at least 15–20 minutes before departure.

blocks.title: If you come on a Monday or Tuesday
blocks.html: Vichayen House is closed Monday and Tuesday, and parts of the museum inside King Narai's Palace have closing days too. If you come early in the week, focus on Phra Prang Sam Yot, Phra Kan Shrine and walking the palace walls instead — you can still fill a fun full day.

blocks.text: What to eat while you walk the old town

blocks.html: Lopburi isn't a flashy food city, but it has local dishes that have been around forever, easy to eat as you wander. The food clusters around the station and the old-town streets. Here's what people tend to go for.

items.name: Chaloem Thai Tom Yum Noodles
items.blurb: An old-school tom yum noodle shop where locals and out-of-towners queue up. Bold flavours and a rich tom yum broth — it's the name people think of first when they talk about eating in Lopburi.

items.name: Boat Noodles at Chai Nam
items.blurb: Punchy boat noodles plus stir-fried dishes, eaten by the Lopburi River where the air is cooler. A good stop if you want to sit and rest a while between sights.

items.name: Rice & curry shops around the station
items.blurb: The area around the station and Narai Maharat Road has plenty of curry-over-rice and made-to-order shops. Prices are friendly and it's ideal for a quick lunch before you start walking.
items.meta: Most open morning–afternoon · Around the station

items.name: Khanom Piak Poon with fresh coconut
items.blurb: A local sweet you'll find at markets and dessert shops in the old town — soft and chewy, topped with sweet, rich coconut cream. Easy to grab and eat on the train ride home.

items.name: Cafes in the old town
items.blurb: Lopburi's old town has several newer cafes, from loft-style spots to garden cafes. Many are within walking distance of the station — good for resting out of the afternoon sun before your train.
items.meta: Several near the station · Open daily

blocks.title: Watch the monkeys when you're carrying food
blocks.html: Lopburi is a genuine monkey town, especially around Phra Prang Sam Yot and Phra Kan Shrine. Don't carry plastic bags, water bottles or food out in the open, and tuck away your glasses, hat and phone. If you want to eat something, do it inside a fenced-off shop — it's much safer.

blocks.text: Tricks to keep this day trip smooth

items: Out early, back in the evening — pick a train that reaches Lopburi before noon and book your return for the evening (around 4–6 pm) so you can sightsee at an easy pace without rushing.

Dress for walking in the sun — the old town involves a lot of open-air walking, so wear comfortable shoes and carry a hat and water — but keep your water tucked away when you pass through monkey zones.
Bring cash — entry fees for the historic sites and many of the old-school shops take cash, so small notes make life easier.
Check opening days — Vichayen House is open Wednesday–Sunday, so if you want to see everything, avoid Monday and Tuesday.
Allow time to reach the station — on the way back, get to the station at least 15–20 minutes before departure so you don't miss your train hunting for a way there.

blocks.html: If a single day leaves you wanting more, Lopburi has plenty to keep you going — Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, the sunflower fields in late and early year, and Khao Jeen Lae, which you'll need a car for. If you want to tick off the lot, stay overnight and then venture out of town. But for a train day trip, the old town around the station fills a day just right.

faq.q: How long does the train from Bangkok to Lopburi take?
faq.a: About 2.5 to 3 hours depending on the train type — express trains are a little quicker than ordinary ones. It's around 150 km, and northern-line trains now mostly leave from Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal (Bang Sue).

faq.q: Can you see Lopburi in a single day round trip?
faq.a: Easily, because Lopburi station sits in the heart of the old town. The main sights — Phra Prang Sam Yot, King Narai's Palace, Vichayen House and Phra Kan Shrine — are all within walking distance of each other. Pick a train that arrives before noon and head back in the evening, and you'll get a full day in.

faq.q: How much is entry to Lopburi's old-town historic sites?
faq.a: For Thais, Phra Prang Sam Yot is 10 THB and King Narai's Palace (Phra Narai Ratchaniwet) is 30 THB, or you can buy a cheaper combined ticket. Foreigners pay more. Bring cash to cover the entry fees.

faq.q: Are the monkeys in Lopburi dangerous?
faq.a: The monkeys are used to people but they're skilled thieves, especially around Phra Prang Sam Yot and Phra Kan Shrine. Don't carry plastic bags, food or drinks out in the open, and tuck away your glasses, hat, phone and bag. Stay alert and you'll be fine.

faq.q: Which days should you avoid visiting Lopburi?
faq.a: If you want to see everything, avoid Monday and Tuesday, since Vichayen House is only open Wednesday–Sunday. Phra Prang Sam Yot and Phra Kan Shrine are open daily, so you can still visit early in the week — you'll just miss a couple of spots.
